meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Max, why are you here?

examples.text: Ты забыла? У вас послезавтра развод!
examples.trans: Did you forget? Your divorce is the day after tomorrow!

examples.text: Знаешь что, давай ты лучше дома переночуешь.
examples.trans: You know what, you had better spend the night at home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They say that thoughts are material.
Yes, did something happen?
Can you bring me something?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'receiver, handset' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты что трубку не берёшь? Всё нормально?
examples.trans: Why are you not picking up the phone? Is everything alright?

Don't hang up!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, do not stay silent.
Can you bring me something?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'do you take/get', paired with 'взять'.

examples.trans: Where are they heading, huh?
There is a chance that everything will work out!
Now your marriage is officially dissolved.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything is fine, girls.
You always ruin everything!

examples.text: Да нет, ребят, тут всё понятно.
examples.trans: No, guys, everything is clear here.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Я нормально. Я сама в неё врезалась. До вечера!
examples.trans: I am fine. I bumped into her myself. Until tonight!

examples.text: Ты что трубку не берёшь? Всё нормально?
examples.trans: Why are you not picking up the phone? Is everything alright?
Everything's fine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They say that thoughts are material.

examples.text: Если о чём-то постоянно думать, это обязательно произойдёт.
examples.trans: If you think about something constantly, it will definitely happen.

examples.text: Звони в любое время! Ладно, я пойду.
examples.trans: Call at any time! Alright, I will go.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'understand', paired with 'понять'.

examples.text: Понимаю, гормоны шалят. Я просто захотела тушёнки!
examples.trans: I understand, hormones are acting up. I simply wanted stewed meat!
Vika, I understand your condition.

examples.text: Я покупал кулон, понимаешь, а не это кольцо!
examples.trans: I bought a pendant, you see, and not this ring!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Лёва, с тебя самая вкусная утка в твоей жизни!
examples.trans: Lyova, the most delicious duck of your life is on you!
Vika, I understand your condition.
Your sister said so.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'остояние'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'condition, state' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Vika, I understand your condition.
Checking the condition of the wall.
In good condition.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если о чём-то постоянно думать, это обязательно произойдёт.
examples.trans: If you think about something constantly, it will definitely happen.
Yes, of course!

examples.text: Сестра недоступна, а самой в магазин идти страшно.
examples.trans: My sister is unreachable, and it is scary to go to the store alone.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'know'.

examples.text: Знаешь что, давай ты лучше дома переночуешь.
examples.trans: You know what, you had better spend the night at home.

examples.text: Кто-нибудь знает, где здесь ближайший ювелирный магазин?
examples.trans: Does anyone know where the nearest jewelry store is around here?

examples.text: Не знаю, в машине лежит диск Агутина.
examples.trans: I do not know, a CD of Agutin is lying in her car.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They say that thoughts are material.
Hello, Vika?
Can you bring me something?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ready').

examples.text: То есть ты подготовил мне сюрприз?
examples.trans: So you prepared a surprise for me?

examples.text: Айнура, приготовь, пожалуйста, к вечеру мой костюм.
examples.trans: Ainura, please get my suit ready for the evening.

examples.text: Но знаешь что? Я во всём готов тебе помогать.
examples.trans: But you know what? I am ready to help you in everything.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'могать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помочь'.

examples.text: Но знаешь что? Я во всём готов тебе помогать.
examples.trans: But you know what? I am ready to help you in everything.
Help Lavrov.
I always help the neighbours.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если о чём-то постоянно думать, это обязательно произойдёт.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'верное').

examples.text: У тебя, наверное, ноги болят, да?
examples.trans: Your legs probably hurt, right?

examples.text: Наверное, массажист. Вика на столе визитку забыла.
examples.trans: Probably a masseur. Vika forgot the business card on the table.
Well, probably somewhere in the archive.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'legs' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У тебя, наверное, ноги болят, да?
examples.trans: Your legs probably hurt, right?
The right foot.
My leg hurts.

meanings.en: to be ill, to be sick
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hurt, ache', paired with 'заболеть'.

examples.trans: My mother is ill.
Your son is ill.

examples.text: Я этого не хочу. Но вспомни, у тебя сын болеет.
examples.trans: I don't want that. But remember, your son is ill.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yes, did something happen?

examples.text: Знаешь что, давай ты лучше дома переночуешь.
examples.trans: You know what, you had better spend the night at home.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'слабиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'relax', paired with 'расслабляться'.

examples.trans: Vanya, relax.
I want to relax.

examples.text: Ваня, расслабься. В этот раз без обмана.
examples.trans: Vanya, relax. This time there's no trick.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you. Sorry that I bothered you.
Thank you for the stewed meat.
Thank you for giving me a ride.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, do not stay silent.

examples.text: Айнура, приготовь, пожалуйста, к вечеру мой костюм.
examples.trans: Ainura, please get my suit ready for the evening.

examples.trans: Can you bring me something?

examples.text: Слушай, ты можешь отключить этот противный звук?
examples.trans: Listen, can you turn off that annoying sound?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Понимаю, гормоны шалят. Я просто захотела тушёнки!
examples.trans: I understand, hormones are acting up. I simply wanted stewed meat!
Chef! I wanted to bring you some tea.

examples.text: Шеф, мы вас ждём. Мы просто хотели, чтобы вы нам помогли.
examples.trans: Chef, we are waiting for you. We just wanted you to help us.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'sex' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Костян, скажи, а правда, что беременным секса больше хочется?
examples.trans: Kostyan, tell me, is it true that pregnant women want sex more?
Well you want sex, do you not?

examples.text: Что-то не похож он на массажиста! Ты сам говорил, что Вике секса хочется.
examples.trans: He does not look like a masseur! You said yourself that Vika wants sex.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'естра'). Common feminine noun meaning 'sister' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Сестра недоступна, а самой в магазин идти страшно.
examples.trans: My sister is unreachable, and it is scary to go to the store alone.

examples.text: Сестра Вики сказала, что Вика хочет.
examples.trans: Vika's sister said that Vika wants it.
Your sister said so.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'told', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Сестра Вики сказала, что Вика хочет.
examples.trans: Vika's sister said that Vika wants it.
Your sister said so.

examples.text: У нас напротив дома тоже написано массажный салон! И этот массажист сказал, что сделает Вике всё очень аккуратно!
examples.trans: Across from our house it also says massage parlor! And this masseur said he would do everything to Vika very carefully!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Таня, мне вечером хватает сил только поесть и помыться.
examples.trans: Tanya, in the evening I only have enough strength to eat and wash up.
Maybe only for a moment.
Lavrov, just not with you!

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Лавров, зайди! Нужен совет. Хочу сделать сюрприз Елене Павловне.
examples.trans: Lavrov, come in! I need advice. I want to make a surprise for Elena Pavlovna.
And who needs this Fedya?

examples.text: Всё, что мне от тебя нужно, — это завтрашний развод!
examples.trans: All that I need from you is tomorrow's divorce!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если о чём-то постоянно думать, это обязательно произойдёт.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втрашний'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tomorrow's').

examples.text: Всё, что мне от тебя нужно, — это завтрашний развод!
examples.trans: All that I need from you is tomorrow's divorce!

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень завтрашний выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very tomorrow's choice.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'divorce, separation' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Всё, что мне от тебя нужно, — это завтрашний развод!
